summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, chronic pain from prior trauma, alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted for cough and alcohol intoxication. He initially expressed willingness to engage in treatment and rehab but became agitated and demanded opioid pain medication. When this was not provided due to safety concerns, he chose to leave against medical advice within an hour of admission. He did not receive treatment for COPD exacerbation or alcohol withdrawal, though breathing treatments provided some symptom relief. He was discharged alert and ambulatory with prescriptions for antibiotics, steroids, blood pressure medications, and vitamins, and urged to follow up and consider rehab. His chest X-ray showed no pneumonia, and blood cultures were negative.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, unspecified
Sedative, hypnotic or anxiolytic abuse, unspecified
Family history of malignant neoplasm of trachea, bronchus, and lung
